Roasted Pork Loin with Apple and Sage

Served at: Twelfth Night

Serves 6-8Prep 20 minCook 60-90 min

Twelfth Night, marking the end of the Christmas season and the eve of Epiphany, is a time for a final festive feast before the return to ordinary time. A succulent roasted pork loin, often served with seasonal fruits like apples and aromatic herbs, makes for a magnificent centerpiece, symbolizing abundance and celebration. This dish is a perfect way to gather family and friends for one last holiday indulgence.

Ingredients

  • 1 (2-3 pound / 0.9-1.4 kg) boneless pork loin roast
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) dried sage
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) dried thyme
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) black pepper
  • 2 medium apples, such as Honeycrisp or Fuji, cored and cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) wedges
  • 1 large onion, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) wedges
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) chicken or apple cider broth

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. Pat the pork loin dry with paper towels.
  3. In a small bowl, combine olive oil, dried sage, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper. Rub the mixture all over the pork loin.
  4. Place the pork loin in a roasting pan. Arrange the apple and onion wedges around the pork.
  5. Pour the chicken or apple cider broth into the bottom of the roasting pan.
  6. Roast for 60-90 minutes, or until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the pork reads 145°F (63°C).
  7. Remove the pork from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, and tent loosely with foil. Let it rest for 10-15 minutes before slicing.
  8. While the pork rests, you can make a pan sauce from the drippings in the roasting pan, if desired, by simmering them on the stovetop.
  9. Slice the pork into 1/2-inch (1.25 cm) thick rounds and serve with the roasted apples and onions, and any pan sauce.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, score the fat cap of the pork loin in a crosshatch pattern before seasoning.
  • Resting the meat is crucial for juicy results; it allows the juices to redistribute throughout the roast.
  • Serve with roasted root vegetables or mashed potatoes for a complete festive meal.
